Kaziranga National Park, located in Assam, is world-famous for its significant population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and plays a critical role in the conservation of this endangered species.

In contrast:

• Bandipur National Park (Karnataka) is known for its tigers and elephants.

• Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand) is India's first national park and known for tigers.

• Gir National Park (Gujarat) is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion.

The Western Ghats run along the western coast of India and pass through the states of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Maharashtra, and a small part of Gujarat.

Madhya Pradesh is located in central India and is not a part of the Western Ghats region.

Hence, it is not encompassed within this biodiversity hotspot.

In contrast:

• Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu have significant areas within the Western Ghats and are known for their rich biodiversity and endemic species.

questions.solution:
Periyar National Park - Kerala

· Established: 1982 (as a National Park; earlier a sanctuary since 1950)

· River: Periyar River

· Details: Located in the Western Ghats, Periyar is famous for its population of wild elephants and the artificial Periyar Lake formed by the Mullaperiyar Dam. The park is rich in biodiversity and also known for eco-tourism activities like bamboo rafting and guided treks.

Gir National Park - Gujarat

· Established: 1975 (as a National Park; sanctuary since 1965)

· River: Hiran River, Shetrunji River, and Datardi River flow through or around the park.

· Details: The only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion in the world, Gir is a dry deciduous forest with a rugged terrain of hills and rivers. It's also home to leopards, antelopes, and marsh crocodiles.

Sunderban National Park - West Bengal

· Established: 1984 (declared as National Park)

· River: Ganges delta rivers, primarily Matla River; part of the larger Sundarbans delta, interspersed with many tidal rivers and creeks.

· Details: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it's the largest tidal halophytic mangrove forest in the world and a critical habitat for the Royal Bengal Tiger. The region is a complex network of waterways and mudflats.

Bandipur National Park - Karnataka

· Established: 1974 (under Project Tiger; originally a sanctuary since 1931)

· River: Kabini River (tributary of the Cauvery River) flows near the park.

· Details: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, Bandipur is known for its dry deciduous forests and grasslands. It's a critical habitat for tigers, elephants, gaurs, and many bird species.

Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary in Odisha is the world's largest known nesting ground for olive ridley sea turtles. Each year, thousands of turtles migrate here for mass nesting, known as arribada.

· Chilika and Pulicat are brackish water lagoons known for migratory birds.

· Point Calimere is known for flamingos and other birds, not sea turtles.

Biodiversity hotspots are areas with a high number of endemic species and overall species richness, but they are also threatened by human activities such as deforestation and habitat destruction.

Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are true, and R correctly explains A.

Namdapha National Park is located in Arunachal Pradesh, which is part of the Eastern Himalayan biodiversity hotspot. It is known for its rich flora and fauna, including several endangered species.

The Eastern Himalayas stretch across northeastern India (Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, northern West Bengal), Bhutan, and parts of Nepal. This region is one of the richest in biodiversity and has been recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot.

· Valley of Flowers is in Uttarakhand (Western Himalayas).

· Kanha (Madhya Pradesh) and Ranthambore (Rajasthan) are not part of the Himalayan region.

Wildlife Sanctuaries are not limited to only animal species. They aim to protect both fauna and flora, i.e., wild animals, birds, and plant life within their natural habitat.

Certain human activities like grazing, tourism, and resource collection may be allowed in sanctuaries, but under strict regulation.

Wildlife sanctuaries are established and managed by the government - either at the state or central level - under the provisions of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

The primary aim of wildlife sanctuaries is to conserve wildlife and their natural habitat, ensuring the survival of endangered and native species.

· Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in Manipur, and it is the only floating national park in the world.

· It is situated on the Loktak Lake, which is famous for its phumdis - masses of floating vegetation.

· This park is the last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer, also known as the dancing deer due to its unique gait.

Further information:

· Keoladeo Ghana National Park - Located in Rajasthan, known for migratory birds, especially Siberian cranes.

· Panna National Park - Located in Madhya Pradesh, famous for tigers and was once declared "tiger-less" before successful reintroduction.

· Dudhwa National Park - Located in Uttar Pradesh, known for swamp deer (barasingha), tigers, and rhinos

A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region that is both:

· Rich in biodiversity (especially endemic species - species found nowhere else), and

· Under significant threat due to habitat loss and human activities.

Further information:

FeatureDescription
1. High Species RichnessContains at least 1,500 endemic plant species (0.5% of global total).
2. EndemismSignificant percentage of species found nowhere else on Earth (e.g., Madagascar's lemurs).
3. Habitat LossMust have lost ≥70% of its original natural vegetation due to human activities (critical threat level).
4. Global PriorityRecognized by international bodies (e.g., Conservation International) for urgent conservation efforts.
5. Threatened SpeciesSupports high numbers of endangered animals/plants (e.g., Western Ghats' lion-tailed macaque).

Examples of Biodiversity Hotspots:

· Western Ghats (India)

· Amazon Rainforest

· Cape Floristic Region (South Africa)

Why Hotspots Matter:

They cover <2.5% of Earth's land but support >50% of endemic plant species and 43% of vertebrates.

questions.solution:
Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary → Saltwater Crocodile

· Location: Odisha

· Why? This sanctuary is famous for having one of the largest populations of saltwater crocodiles in India. It's a key mangrove ecosystem and an important habitat for estuarine species.

Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary → Sloth Bear

· Location: Karnataka

· Why? This is India's first sanctuary dedicated solely to sloth bears. The rocky terrain here is ideal for their habitat, and it's a hotspot for sloth bear conservation.

Dachigam National Park → Hangul

· Location: Jammu & Kashmir

· Why? Dachigam is the only place in the world where the Hangul (Kashmir Stag) is found in the wild. It's a critically endangered species and a focus of conservation in this region.

Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary → Grizzled Giant Squirrel

· Location: Kerala (bordering Tamil Nadu)

· Why? One of the few places in India where you can spot the Grizzled Giant Squirrel, a rare and endangered species with a distinct long tail and large size.

The Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot spans the Indo-Burmese border and covers parts of northeastern India, Myanmar, and Southeast Asia.

It is known for high species richness and endemism, but is also critically threatened by human activities.

In contrast:

· Western Ghats are on India's west coast.

· Sundaland includes the Nicobar Islands and parts of Southeast Asia.

· Himalaya hotspot spans the entire Himalayan range.

Ranthambore National Park is located in Rajasthan and is one of the most prominent tiger reserves in India.

· Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh,

· Corbett in Uttarakhand,

· Bandipur in Karnataka.

The boundaries of a Wildlife Sanctuary are always well-defined and cannot be altered. This is false because the boundaries of Wildlife Sanctuaries can indeed be altered through proper legal procedures. Unlike the statement suggests, their boundaries are not permanently fixed and can be modified by the government if necessary.

The other statements are correct:

National Parks do have a higher degree of protection compared to Wildlife Sanctuaries under India's wildlife protection laws.

Wildlife Sanctuaries do allow certain regulated human activities (like grazing, harvesting forest produce, etc.) while National Parks generally prohibit most human activities except tourism and research.

National Parks are established with the goal of protecting entire ecosystems including flora, fauna, landscape and habitat, while Wildlife Sanctuaries can be designated to protect particular species or groups of species.

The Sundarbans is part of the Sundaland Biodiversity Hotspot, which includes the Nicobar Islands (but not the Andaman Islands), the Malay Peninsula, Borneo, Java, Sumatra, and surrounding smaller islands.

It is famous for its mangrove forests, Royal Bengal Tigers, and rich aquatic and terrestrial biodiversity.

Campbell Bay National Park is in Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The others are located in mainland India:

· Silent Valley (Kerala),

· Eravikulam (Kerala),

· Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu).

· Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary is located in Haryana, approximately 40 km from Delhi, making it the nearest bird sanctuary to the national capital.

· It is a popular destination for bird watchers, especially in winter, as it hosts migratory birds from Europe, Siberia, and Central Asia.

· Nal Sarovar Bird Sanctuary - Located in Gujarat, near Ahmedabad.

· Chilika Bird Sanctuary - Located in Odisha, near the Chilika Lake.

The largest protected area in India is the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve.

This tiger reserve, located in the state of Andhra Pradesh, covers approximately 3,568 square kilometers (1,378 square miles) and is the largest tiger reserve in India. It's situated in the Nallamala Hills and is named after the Nagarjunasagar Dam and the Srisailam temple located within its boundaries.

The other options are significant protected areas but smaller in size:

· Hemis National Park is in Ladakh

· Desert National Park is in Rajasthan

· Manas National Park is in Assam

Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, known for tigers, leopards, elephants, and rich biodiversity.

The other sanctuaries are in different states:

· Periyar - Kerala

· Mudumalai - Tamil Nadu

· Thattekad - Kerala

· Sundaland is one of the four recognized biodiversity hotspots in India.

· It includes the Nicobar Islands, along with parts of Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, and southern Thailand.

· Andaman Islands, on the other hand, are not part of any hotspot, but the Nicobar Islands specifically fall under Sundaland due to their distinct flora and fauna influenced by Southeast Asian biogeography.

Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary is a large shallow wetland located in the northeastern region of Uthukuli Taluk, Tiruppur District, Tamil Nadu.

Situated about 10 km north of Tiruppur city along the Tiruppur-Uthukkuli main road, the lake spans 125.865 hectares and lies between the villages of Sarkar Periyapalayam and Neruperichal. It was historically restored by King Nanjarayan, from whom it derives its name.

The sanctuary supports a rich biodiversity, with 191 bird species, 87 butterfly species, 7 amphibians, 21 reptiles, 11 small mammals, and 77 plant species recorded.

Further, it serves as a crucial feeding and nesting ground for resident and migratory birds and is a vital water source for local agriculture.

The other options are located in different states:

· Ashtamudi Lake is in Kerala

· Deepor Beel is in Assam

· Bhoj Wetlands are in Madhya Pradesh

As of February 2025, there are 89 Ramsar sites in India, including bird sanctuaries, wetlands, and wildlife sanctuaries.

Wetlands are critical ecosystems that play an imperative role in maintaining ecological balance, supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services essential for human survival.

The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, an international treaty established in 1971, provides the framework for the conservation and wise use of wetlands globally.
